summary:
Held 1 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 5 upside misses — ASM.AS +6%, UNA.AS +5%, JD.L +4%, ADM.L +4%, STMPA.PA +4%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (HLMA.L -15%, DSY.PA -8%, SAP.DE -6%, CAP.PA -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: HLMA.L (-15.38%) — Full-year FY2026 results beat on revenue (£2.58B, +15%) and EBIT, but FY2027 guidance cut to 'low double-digit' growth vs 16.2% organic in FY2026, and single-customer concentration in Photonics rising to 20% of group sales triggered a sharp derating. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — HLMA.L is a FTSE-100 large-cap industrial/safety-tech conglomerate, likely above the liquidity-normalised cap tier the momentum and mean-reversion strategies target. The move was entirely results-day driven; any signal would only appear post-open, by which time >10% of the gap h

top_movers.catalyst: Stacked broker upgrades: Berenberg lifted PT to €240 from €140 on Jun 10 citing AI hybrid bonding ramp; BofA raised target ~Jun 12 — compounding analyst momentum into a +6.9% gap on heavy AEX volume.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BESI (€23B AEX semiconductor equipment, GICS 45301020) is not in macro-aligned's or any other strategy's coverage list, so no technical filter was even reached; the move was structurally invisible.
top_movers.suggestion: Extend macro-aligned's universe to include AEX large-cap semis equipment (mkt-cap >€5B, GICS 45301020); add a multi-broker-upgrade entry gate (≥2 PT raises within 5 sessions) to limit churn and target analyst-momentum setups like this one.

top_movers.catalyst: Delayed sector spillover from ASML's Terafab/Elon Musk-driven rally (Jun 8–11 +~10%); ASM International's own Q1 2026 beat (€862M rev, record 33.1% op margin) provided fundamental support for the re-rating.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely. ASM.AS is a high-priced (~€961), large-cap (~€45B) Dutch semiconductor equipment name; the move was a sector rotation spillover requiring a peer-correlation link to ASML — not a detectable pre-market signal in an isolated single-name screener.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'semicon-equipment sector contagion' rule: when ASML.AS closes >+3% on day T, expand the next-open universe to include correlated AEX/Euronext semiconductor equipment peers (ASM, BESI) with a 1-session lookback gate.

Oracle capex-shock contagion unfolded across two sessions; capturing it required pre-earnings positioning in a US peer before EU open.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a peer-contagion overlay: when a major US ERP/cloud peer (Oracle, Salesforce) gaps ≤ −8% post-earnings, flag SAP.DE as a short candidate at next EU open requiring ≥1.2× avg volume in the first 30 min before entry.

top_movers.catalyst: European tech-sector contagion from Broadcom's AI-chip warning (~June 5) compounded Capgemini's post-CMD guidance miss (FCF €1.8-1.9B vs ~€2B est) and a cluster of analyst PT cuts; no discrete June 12 release identified.

top_movers.suggestion: If a sector-pairs strategy is ever added, include EU large-cap IT services (CAP, DSY, ATO) on the short leg triggered by post-CMD FCF guidance misses ≥5%; until then, no actionable change — this requires short capability the current book lacks.
